In this study, we investigated significant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for anti\u2010HBs antibody levels in 6867 healthy Koreans using a genome\u2010wide association study (GWAS). In GWAS, the top 20 SNPs that showed significant association with anti\u2010HBs levels (<jats:italic>P<\/jats:italic>\u00a0<\u00a01.0\u00a0\u00d7\u00a010<jats:sup>\u221229<\/jats:sup>) all resided in <jats:italic>HLA\u2010DPB1<\/jats:italic>. Utilizing PCR sequencing, we verified the relationship of the top 3 most significant SNPs (rs1042169, rs9277355 and rs9277356) from the GWAS and genotypes of <jats:italic>HLA\u2010DPB1<\/jats:italic> with the HB vaccine response in Korean infants who received a scheduled vaccination. The <jats:italic>DPB1*04:02<\/jats:italic> allele has G, C and A nucleotides for the 3SNP sites, and was significantly more frequent in responders than in nonresponders (10.9% vs 1.0%, <jats:italic>P<jats:sub>c<\/jats:sub><\/jats:italic>\u00a0=\u00a00.018). <jats:italic>DPB1*05:01<\/jats:italic> was significantly more frequent in nonresponders than in responders (49.0% vs 31.1%, <jats:italic>P<jats:sub>c<\/jats:sub><\/jats:italic>\u00a0=\u00a00.018). In multivariate logistic regression, <jats:italic>DPB1*04:02<\/jats:italic> showed a significant association with both vaccine response (<jats:italic>P<\/jats:italic>\u00a0=\u00a00.037, OR\u00a0=\u00a08.465) and high\u2010titre response (<jats:italic>P<\/jats:italic>\u00a0=\u00a00.027, OR\u00a0=\u00a09.860). The haplotypes rs1042169 G \u2010 rs9277355 C \u2010 rs9277356 A showed a significant association with a high\u2010titre response only (<jats:italic>P<\/jats:italic>\u00a0=\u00a00.002, OR\u00a0=\u00a02.941). In conclusion, <jats:italic>DPB1*04:02<\/jats:italic> possessing rs1042169 G \u2010 rs9277355 C \u2010 rs9277356 A is an independent predictor of the HB vaccine response in
